[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"MK-ULTRA: what survived the shredder","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"MK-ULTRA (1953–1973) is the bedrock documented case. CIA Director Richard Helms ordered all files destroyed in 1973; approximately **20,000 pages survived** only because they had been incorrectly stored in a financial records building rather than the project files location. They were discovered via a 1977 FOIA request by journalist John Marks. These documents, supplemented by the 1975 Church Committee hearings and the 1977 Senate Select Committee hearings, reveal **149 documented subprojects across 80 institutions**: 44 colleges and universities, 15 research foundations or pharmaceutical companies, 12 hospitals and clinics, involving 185 identified non-government researchers.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Sidney Gottlieb headed the program. His recently fully declassified Church Committee testimony (published by the National Security Archive, October 2025) reveals he acknowledged the program had \"as many failures as successes\" and concluded \"the money expended, the effort expended, the security risk involved... it was probably not a high pay-off program.\" The program funded research into LSD, mescaline, hypnosis, sensory deprivation, verbal and sexual abuse, and other methods of behavioral control.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Ted Kaczynski connection is documented but more limited than often claimed. Kaczynski entered Harvard at 16 and participated (1959–1962) in a study led by Professor Henry Murray, who had worked for the OSS during WWII developing interrogation techniques. Murray described his own sessions as \"vehement, sweeping, and personally abusive.\" Kaczynski spent approximately 200 hours in the study. **Whether Murray's specific study was MK-ULTRA-funded cannot be confirmed** — the relevant records were destroyed. Kaczynski himself disputed the connection from prison, writing that the experience \"could not have been described as 'torture' even in the loosest sense of the word.\"","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Thread 2: Anton LaVey — the showman and the substance behind the spectacle","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The documented man vs. the constructed legend","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Anton LaVey (born **Howard Stanton Levey**, April 11, 1930, Chicago) was perhaps the most accomplished self-mythologizer in American religious history. Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Lawrence Wright conducted the most rigorous independent investigation (Rolling Stone, 1991), and LaVey's own estranged daughter Zeena Schreck published corroborating findings in 1998. Most recently, Doug Brod's *Born with a Tail* (2024, Hachette) drew on 50+ interviews and archival research.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The results are damning for LaVey's autobiography. He claimed to have joined the Clyde Beatty Circus at 16 — **no evidence found** in circus route books. He claimed an affair with Marilyn Monroe — **debunked** by the manager of the theater where Monroe allegedly danced. He claimed to have played oboe in the San Francisco Ballet Orchestra — **no evidence found**. He claimed to have worked as an SFPD crime scene photographer — SFPD stated \"no one named Howard or Anton LaVey or Levey ever worked for the force.\" His grandmother was Ukrainian, not \"a Gypsy from Transylvania.\" The Black House was his parents' home, not a former brothel.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"What *was* real: LaVey was a genuinely talented keyboardist (well-attested by multiple sources), did play organ at the Lost Weekend nightclub and San Francisco Civic Auditorium, and possessed undeniable charisma and showmanship. Wright's elegant assessment: \"Anton LaVey is an imaginary creation, as real, and as false, as a soap-opera character or a comic-book anti-hero.\" Brod called him \"one part pope, nine parts P.T. Barnum.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Hollywood connections that are real","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Sammy Davis Jr.** — documented in Davis's own 1989 autobiography and corroborated by a 2024 Rolling Stone investigation. Davis attended Church of Satan gatherings from approximately 1968–1974, wore a painted red fingernail (a Church signifier), and received the honorary title \"Warlock II.\" He described his introduction through actors at The Factory nightclub and characterized events as \"dungeons and dragons and debauchery.\" He departed around 1974 calling it \"a short-lived interest.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Jayne Mansfield** — documented through extensive photographic evidence (German paparazzo Walter Fischer, published in *California Infernal*, 2017). She visited the Black House in October 1966, received a medallion, and was dubbed \"High Priestess.\" The nature of the relationship was mutually advantageous publicity. The famous \"curse\" story — LaVey allegedly cursing Mansfield's boyfriend Sam Brody, who then died alongside her in a June 1967 car accident — comes primarily from Church of Satan sources. The accident was a mundane rear-ending of a tractor-trailer in darkness.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Kenneth Anger** — documented longtime friend, part of LaVey's pre-Church \"Magic Circle.\" LaVey appeared in Anger's *Invocation of My Demon Brother* (1969). Anger briefly served as a Church of Satan priest.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"LaVey's most persistent Hollywood claim — that he served as **technical advisor on *Rosemary's Baby* and played the Devil** — is **thoroughly debunked**. Producer Gene Gutowski stated LaVey never met Polanski. The Devil was played by actor Clay Tanner, confirmed by Paramount's cast records and on-set photographs. Even LaVey's former son-in-law Nikolas Schreck, himself a self-described Satanist, called this a fabrication. LaVey's only actual connection was appearing at the San Francisco premiere as a promotional gimmick. He did genuinely serve as technical advisor on the completely different, low-budget *The Devil's Rain* (1975).","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Satanic Bible: a derivative but influential text","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Published by Avon Books in 1969 (commissioned after the success of *Rosemary's Baby*), *The Satanic Bible* has sold over **600,000 copies** across 30+ printings — far exceeding actual Church membership, which never surpassed roughly 2,000. Its philosophical sources are well-documented: Ayn Rand's ethical egoism (LaVey himself stated \"LaVeyan Satanism was just Ayn Rand's philosophy, with ceremony and ritual added\"), Nietzsche's master-slave morality, and substantial sections copied nearly verbatim from **Ragnar Redbeard's** *Might Is Right* (1896) — a social Darwinist tract from which LaVey edited out the explicit racism and antisemitism. Enochian keys were adapted from Crowley with Satanic substitutions.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Church's cultural function was dual: genuine philosophical framework (atheistic Satanism treating rituals as psychological psychodramas) and deliberate media spectacle. LaVey staged the first public Satanic wedding, baptism, and funeral, all designed for maximum press coverage. He appeared on *The Tonight Show*, *Donahue*, and was covered by *Time*, *Newsweek*, and *Cosmopolitan*. Sociologist James R. Lewis found that 60% of Church members viewed Satan as symbol rather than entity, and 20% cited *The Satanic Bible* itself as their primary attraction.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Intelligence connections: what the record shows","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"FBI files on LaVey have been released via FOIA (approximately 55 pages, partially redacted). The most substantive entry documents a 1980 investigation into an alleged plot to assassinate Senator Ted Kennedy — which FBI and Secret Service quickly determined LaVey had no involvement in. During the investigation, agents reported LaVey's \"interest in the Church of Satan is strictly from a monetary point of view.\" The files also contain bomb threats *against* the Church and foreign law enforcement inquiries.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**No documented direct connection between LaVey and CIA or military intelligence has been established.** Claims to this effect come from conspiracy-oriented sources lacking primary documentation. The documented geographic overlap between LaVey's San Francisco milieu and CIA operations (MK-ULTRA, the counterculture penetration programs) is real but does not constitute organizational connection.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"---","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Key Traditions Converging on Self-Identity","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Kashmir Shaivism:** *Aham vimarśa*, *spanda*, Śiva-Śakti as the mono-poly. The recognition (*pratyabhijñā*) tradition: Self-Identity recognising itself.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Advaita Vedanta:** *Tat tvam asi*, *neti neti*, the Self as *sat-cit-ānanda*","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Meister Eckhart:** The ground of the soul IS the ground of God. \"The eye with which I see God...\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Cusanus:** *Coincidentia oppositorum*, the circle without circumference, learned ignorance","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Whitehead:** Concrescence — the many become one and are increased by one","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Jung:** The Self archetype, the *complexio oppositorum*, individuation, the psychoid nature of number (with Pauli)","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Kastrup:** Analytic idealism — reality as fundamentally experiential, one mind, many expressions","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Origen:** *Apokatastasis* — all minds return to the source, because the source IS the mind","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Gödel / Hofstadter:** Self-reference as the generative engine of both paradox and consciousness","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Pythagoras:** The perfect number (6 = 1+2+3 = 1×2×3), the tetraktys, the music of number","styles":{}}]},{"type":"bulletListItem","content":[{"type":"text","text":"***Liber XXIV Philosophorum*:** \"God is a circle whose centre is everywhere and circumference nowhere\"","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Occult as technology: the Bernays parallel","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The most analytically productive framework for understanding this material is not \"do powerful people secretly worship Satan?\" but rather: **how does the technology of perception management relate to the technology of ritual?** Aquino's framework provides the clearest articulation. His Lesser Black Magic explicitly encompassed politics and propaganda. His MindWar paper explicitly referenced \"the esoteric arts of antiquity\" alongside science and psychology. He treated magical practice as applied psychology focused on manipulating perceptions — which is precisely what PSYOP doctrine does.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"But Aquino was not the first to articulate this parallel. **Edward Bernays** wrote in *Propaganda* (1928): \"The conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organized habits and opinions of the masses is an important element in democratic society. Those who manipulate this unseen mechanism of society constitute an invisible government which is the true ruling power of our country.\" Bernays' \"engineering of consent\" used Freudian insights about unconscious desires to reshape behavior through symbolic action — the \"Torches of Freedom\" campaign reframing women's smoking as feminist liberation is a textbook case of what an occultist might call sympathetic magic translated into advertising. Walter Lippmann's *Public Opinion* (1922) had already established that the public operates on \"pictures in their heads\" rather than direct reality. Jacques Ellul's *Propaganda* (1962) argued that propaganda is an inescapable feature of technological society — and Aquino explicitly cited Ellul in the MindWar paper.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The structural parallel is real: **both occult ritual and modern propaganda systematically use symbols, narrative, and environmental manipulation to reshape consciousness in ways the target may not consciously recognize.** The difference is that propaganda theory developed from Enlightenment psychology and mass communication research, while occult practice draws on pre-modern initiatory traditions. Aquino is the documented figure who most explicitly bridged these two streams.","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Jack Parsons: the documented nexus of rocketry, occultism, and science fiction","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Jack Parsons (1914–1952) represents the most extraordinary documented case of simultaneous participation in military-industrial technology and active occult practice. He co-founded both the **Jet Propulsion Laboratory** and **Aerojet Engineering Corporation**, invented the first castable composite solid rocket propellant (foundational technology for the Space Shuttle boosters and Minuteman missiles), and has a lunar crater named after him. He had no college degree.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Parsons discovered Thelema through reading Aleister Crowley, joined the O.T.O.'s **Agape Lodge** in Pasadena around 1939, and became its head. He turned his mansion at 1003 South Orange Grove Avenue (\"The Parsonage\") into a bohemian commune, reportedly chanting Crowley's \"Hymn to Pan\" before rocket test launches. His social circle overlapped with the early science fiction community: he was friends with Robert Heinlein, attended meetings at Heinlein's Laurel Canyon home, and knew a teenage Ray Bradbury through the Los Angeles Science Fantasy Society. **Rocketry, occultism, and science fiction were not separate worlds in 1940s Pasadena — they were overlapping communities with the Parsonage as a literal nexus point.**","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The **Babalon Working** (January–March 1946) is documented through Parsons' letters, Crowley's correspondence, and a peer-reviewed academic analysis by Henrik Bogdan in *Numen* (2016). L. Ron Hubbard moved into the Parsonage in August 1945; Parsons wrote to Crowley that Hubbard was \"the most Thelemic person I have ever met.\" Hubbard served as \"Scribe\" during rituals involving Enochian magic. Upon the arrival of Marjorie Cameron — a former Navy WAVE — Parsons believed her to be the \"elemental\" woman he had invoked. Parsons then performed sex magic rituals with Cameron while Hubbard continued as assistant, and believed he received *Liber 49* via psychographic transmission.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Crowley's reaction is documented**: \"fairly frantic when I contemplate the idiocy of these louts!\" The Church of Scientology later claimed (1969) that Hubbard had been \"sent in\" by the U.S. government to \"break up Black Magic in America.\" This claim is contradicted by court testimony from Gerry Armstrong, Scientology's own former archivist, who stated under oath that he found the Naval Intelligence story was authored by Hubbard himself and that \"Mr. Hubbard was not working for Naval intelligence; was, in fact, connected to the OTO.\" After the Working, Hubbard defrauded Parsons of approximately **$20,000** and absconded with his ex-girlfriend Sara Northrup.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Parsons died on June 17, 1952, in an explosion in his home laboratory while preparing pyrotechnics for a film industry rush order. His right forearm was severed and his legs and left arm broken. He was found conscious; his reported last words were \"But I'm not finished yet.\" The official finding was accidental dropping of fulminate of mercury. Colleagues called him \"extremely safety-conscious.\" His mother took a fatal overdose of barbiturates upon hearing the news. The circumstances remain genuinely ambiguous.","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Oxford, Ruskin, and the intellectual architecture of supremacism","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Rhodes matriculated at Oriel College, Oxford, on October 13, 1873 — three years after arriving in Africa, already a working diamond miner. He was older than typical undergraduates, wealthier from trade (a socially suspect source), and frequently absent. He would pass around a small box of diamonds in class. He shuttled between Kimberley and Oxford for eight years, finally taking his BA in 1881 — almost certainly a Pass degree rather than Honours, given his intermittent attendance. His determination to get the degree was driven by a specific conviction: \"Wherever you turn your eye — except in science — an Oxford man is at the top of the tree.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Oriel in the 1870s was past its intellectual prime. Once the cradle of the Oxford Movement, it was now \"better known for prowess at rowing, football and cricket than in final exams.\" But the broader Oxford atmosphere was fermenting with imperial ideology. The key influences on Rhodes were layered and reinforcing:","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**John Ruskin's inaugural lecture** as Slade Professor of Fine Art, delivered February 8, 1870, to an overflow crowd at the Sheldonian Theatre, contained a passage that became Rhodes's ideological lodestar: \"There is a destiny now possible to us — the highest ever set before a nation to be accepted or refused. We are still undegenerate in race; a race mingled of the best northern blood... She must found colonies as fast and as far as she is able, formed of her most energetic and worthiest men; seizing every piece of fruitful waste ground she can set her foot on.\" Rhodes almost certainly did **not** attend this lecture — he was in England but did not arrive at Oxford until 1873. He encountered the published text, issued by Clarendon Press in 1872. Carroll Quigley's claim that Rhodes \"copied it out in longhand and kept it with him for thirty years\" lacks independent verification, but the ideological parallels are unmistakable: Ruskin's \"found colonies... formed of her most energetic and worthiest men\" maps directly onto Rhodes's \"secret society\" of the ablest.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Winwood Reade's *The Martyrdom of Man*** (1872) was, by Rhodes's own testimony, the most transformative single text. \"It made me what I am,\" he told associates. This controversial universal history applied Darwinian evolution to civilization, arguing that war, slavery, and religion were necessary developmental stages to be superseded by science. It was denounced by Gladstone as dangerously irreligious. For Rhodes, it provided the framework for replacing Christian faith with a secular religion of racial progress — and it centered Africa in the story of human development.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Aristotle's concept of *megalopsychia*** — greatness of soul — appears twice in the Confession, where Rhodes laments that men possessing this quality lack the organizational channel to exercise it. **Marcus Aurelius's Stoic ethics** of duty and self-mastery remained his constant companion. **Gibbon's imperial narrative** provided the template of civilizational rise and fall. **Charles Dilke's *Greater Britain*** (1868), a bestselling travelogue, introduced the concept of a global Anglo-Saxon community: \"I followed England round the world... the grandeur of our race, already girding the earth.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The intellectual atmosphere of 1870s Oxford combined all these currents. The Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71 had intensified British anxiety about national power. Social Darwinism was ascendant. The historian Edward Augustus Freeman was articulating Anglo-Saxon racial historiography. Benjamin Jowett, Master of Balliol, preached his desire to \"inoculate the world\" with Oxford-educated leaders. The \"New Imperialism\" — a shift from mid-Victorian ambivalence to active enthusiasm for expansion — was gathering force.","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Rudolf II's Prague: where alchemy met astronomy","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before the catastrophe, one Habsburg court had embodied a different possibility. Rudolf II (Emperor 1576–1612) moved his capital from Vienna to Prague in 1583, creating one of the most extraordinary intellectual environments in European history. His court hosted **Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler** (both Protestants, evidence of Rudolf's religious tolerance), the English occultist John Dee and his associate Edward Kelley, the philosopher Giordano Bruno, and numerous alchemists including Michael Sendivogius. Rudolf personally sought the philosopher's stone and maintained a private alchemy laboratory.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"His *Kunstkammer* — nine rooms in Prague Castle housing art, exotic animals, minerals, automata, and curiosities — was described as \"unrivaled and one of the most diverse of its time.\" The surviving 1607–1611 inventory documents this encyclopedic collection. Rudolf \"viewed his Kunstkammer as the centre of his political world, his treasures an extension of his rule and power,\" according to Thomas DaCosta Kaufmann, the leading scholar on this topic.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**A documented lineage connects Medici esoteric patronage to Habsburg Prague.** The 1565 marriage of Francesco I de' Medici to Habsburg Archduchess Johanna of Austria was, as Courtauld Institute research has established, \"a catalytic event that brought the German-speaking dominions of Central Europe into close contact with Florence, its court and its multifaceted arts.\" The Italian *studiolo* — exemplified by Francesco I de' Medici's studiolo in the Palazzo Vecchio (completed 1570–72) — is recognized as a direct precursor to the northern European Kunstkammer. The conceptual framework was identical: encyclopedic universal collections blending art, nature, and science. Ambassador networks facilitated continuous exchange of art objects, rare gems, and exotic animals between Italian and Habsburg courts. The Hermetic intellectual tradition that had flourished under the Medici — Marsilio Ficino's translations of the Hermetic Corpus for Cosimo de' Medici in the 1460s — provided the shared philosophical substrate for both collecting traditions. Active academic research continues on these connections through the \"Collecting Central Europe\" scholarly network coordinating the Courtauld, Czech Academy of Sciences, and other institutions. This is mainstream art-historical scholarship, not fringe.","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Thread 1: Michael Aquino — the man who wrote PSYOP doctrine and founded a temple","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The military career","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Michael A. Aquino Jr. (1946–2019) earned a B.A. in political science from UC Santa Barbara in 1968 as a Distinguished Military Graduate, receiving a Regular Army commission. He served in Vietnam as a psychological operations officer, deploying loudspeaker-equipped helicopters to broadcast psychologically disorienting audio over enemy positions. One documented operation exploited Vietnamese-Buddhist burial customs: a recording of funeral music transitioning into screams of a soldier \"dragged away by demons,\" broadcast from above cloud cover during thunderstorms. He received the Bronze Star, Air Medal, and Republic of Vietnam Gallantry Cross.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"After Vietnam, Aquino's career trajectory is documented through court records and his own CV: he served as Research & Analysis Team Leader at the 7th PSYOP Group at the Presidio of San Francisco, held a reserve attaché position at the **Defense Intelligence Agency** in 1981, attended the Defense Intelligence College and Foreign Service Institute, and completed the Industrial College of the Armed Forces at National Defense University. His positions would have required at minimum a **Top Secret/SCI clearance** — standard for DIA personnel — though the specific clearance level has not been independently confirmed from declassified primary documents. He retired as Lieutenant Colonel in 1994.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"MindWar: what the paper actually says","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"\"From PSYOP to MindWar: The Psychology of Victory\" (1980), co-authored with Colonel Paul E. Vallely (Commander, 7th PSYOP Group), was an unofficial internal \"talking paper\" — not classified, not formal doctrine, not an official policy document. Vallely circulated it to stimulate dialogue within PSYOP commands. Its core argument was radical: **psychological operations should become the primary instrument of warfare**, not a force-multiplier for conventional arms. \"The advantage of MindWar is that it conducts wars in nonlethal, noninjurious, and nondestructive ways. Essentially you overwhelm your enemy with argument.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The paper's most controversial dimension is its stance on targeting friendly populations. It explicitly states: **\"MindWar must target all participants if it is to be effective. It must not only weaken the enemy; it must strengthen the United States.\"** It then acknowledges that existing law prohibits PSYOP units from targeting American citizens, but argues this prohibition rests on the \"presumption that 'propaganda' is necessarily a lie\" — and since MindWar \"always speaks the truth,\" it would be something categorically different. Critics have noted the rhetorical sleight of hand: Aquino simultaneously acknowledges the legal prohibition while arguing for its circumvention through semantic redefinition.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Three extended footnotes address technological enhancement of psychological operations. The paper references atmospheric electromagnetic activity and its effects on human cognition, air ionization (negative ions enhancing alertness, positive ions inducing drowsiness), and most notably **Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) waves**: \"ELF-waves are not normally noticed by the unaided senses, yet their resonant effect upon the human body has been connected to both physiological disorders and emotional distortion. Infrasound could be used tactically... and it could be used in conjunction with media broadcasts as well.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"MindWar was never adopted as official doctrine. But in his 2003 introduction, Aquino noted that Gulf War I and the 2003 Iraq invasion both applied MindWar principles — including journalist embedding, which \"inevitably channel[ed] their perspectives and perceptions.\" Some of its core concepts (information dominance, media-centric warfare, perception management) have clear parallels in later military doctrine on information operations, though no direct doctrinal lineage has been established.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The occult career and the split with LaVey","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Aquino joined the Church of Satan in 1969 after encountering an advertisement in the *Berkeley Barb*. During Vietnam, he corresponded with Anton LaVey. By 1973, he held the rank of Magister Templi IV° — the highest achievable rank below LaVey's own — serving as editor of the Church newsletter *The Cloven Hoof* and sitting on the governing Council of Nine. He was effectively LaVey's right-hand man.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The 1975 split involved multiple fault lines. LaVey had begun **selling priesthoods for cash**, which Aquino viewed as betraying meritocratic principles. More fundamentally, the two men held irreconcilable metaphysical positions: LaVey was essentially an atheist who treated Satan as a symbolic archetype; **Aquino was a theist who believed in a literal preternatural entity**. On the North Solstice of 1975, Aquino performed a ritual and produced *The Book of Coming Forth by Night* — which he described as received through a process resembling automatic writing — in which Set (the Egyptian deity) proclaimed the beginning of a new Aeon and raised Aquino to the rank of Magus V°. He took approximately 100 followers (LaVey dismissively claimed only 29) to found the Temple of Set.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Temple of Set taught that Set gave humanity the \"Black Flame\" — a questioning intellect providing \"isolate self-consciousness\" distinguishing humans from animals. The goal was **Xeper** (Egyptian: \"I Have Come Into Being\"), a process of radical self-transformation toward self-deification. The organization peaked at roughly **500 members** around 1984, maintained a six-degree initiatory system, and operated specialized internal orders including the Order of the Trapezoid. It continues to exist with a low public profile.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Wewelsburg Working","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"On October 19, 1982, while in Europe for NATO-related military duties, Aquino performed a ritual he called \"The Wewelsburg Working\" in the Hall of the Dead (Walhalla) in the North Tower of Wewelsburg Castle — the castle Heinrich Himmler had intended as a ceremonial center for the SS. The castle was then functioning as a youth hostel and small museum. Aquino's stated purpose was \"to summon the Powers of Darkness at their most powerful locus\" and to reconstitute the **Order of the Trapezoid** as a formal sub-order of the Temple of Set.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Aquino's relationship to Nazi esotericism was what historian Nevill Drury described as a conviction that \"the Nazis were able to summon an extraordinary psychic force which was misdirected — but need not have been.\" He had published an article titled \"That Other Black Order\" in *The Cloven Hoof* in 1972, demonstrating longstanding interest in SS mysticism. True-crime reporter Michael Newton described Aquino's public stance on the Reich as \"deliberately ambiguous.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Presidio allegations","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Presidio case must be handled with particular epistemological care. **What is documented from court records** (*Aquino v. Stone*, 957 F.2d 139, 4th Cir. 1992) and investigative journalism: In November 1986, investigations began into Gary Hambright, a civilian daycare worker at the Presidio Army Base, for child sexual abuse. In August 1987, the case expanded when Captain Larry Adams-Thompson's three-year-old daughter identified Aquino as \"Mikey\" — a name she had used in earlier therapy sessions. Investigators raided the Aquinos' residence, seizing videotapes, photographs, and costume materials.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Documented physical evidence**: at least four children (ages 3–7) tested positive for chlamydia. More than 60 children were eventually involved in allegations. **Legal outcome**: Aquino was **never formally charged** by either civilian or military authorities. SFPD discontinued its investigation in September 1988 citing insufficient evidence. However, the Army CID **refused to remove Aquino's name** from its investigation report, stating \"the evidence of alibi offered by LTC Aquino [was] not persuasive.\" The Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals upheld this finding, ruling there was \"sufficient evidence from which the Army decision maker could determine that probable cause existed.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The case exists in genuine epistemological limbo. It occurred during the nationwide \"Satanic Ritual Abuse\" moral panic, when numerous daycare centers faced allegations later found unfounded (McMartin, etc.), and interviewing techniques of the era have been heavily criticized. But the physical evidence (chlamydia in children) is documented and real. Aquino maintained his innocence until death, publishing *Extreme Prejudice: The Presidio \"Satanic Abuse\" Scam*. **Neither guilt nor innocence was conclusively established.**","styles":{}}]},{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The conceptual bridge: Lesser Black Magic and PSYOP doctrine","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The most analytically significant aspect of Aquino's career is the parallel between his occult taxonomy and military doctrine. His concept of **Lesser Black Magic** — \"impelling things in the objective universe to perform desired acts by using obscure physical or behavioral laws,\" into which he explicitly placed politics and propaganda — maps remarkably onto PSYOP principles: systematic study of target psychology, manipulation of perceptions through crafted messaging, use of environmental factors to enhance suggestibility, and strategic application of influence without the target's awareness. **Greater Black Magic** — transformation of the self through ritual — maps onto the operator's own training and initiation.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Whether the occult practice informed the military doctrine or vice versa cannot be determined. The chronological overlap (Aquino developed both simultaneously throughout the 1970s–80s) makes disentangling causation impossible. What is documented is that he explicitly referenced \"the esoteric arts of antiquity\" alongside science and psychology in his 2013 expanded *MindWar* book.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"---","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The academic framework for occultation","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Wouter Hanegraaff, Professor of History of Hermetic Philosophy at the University of Amsterdam, provides the most rigorous scholarly treatment of this thesis. In *Esotericism and the Academy* (2012), he argues that Protestant theologians and Enlightenment scholars \"joined hands to proclaim their own modern rationality while relegating esoteric currents of thought to the 'waste-basket' of history.\" This was a process of **mnemohistory** — what a culture imagines happened rather than what actually did. Esoteric traditions became \"the Other by which academics define their own identity to the present day.\"","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Jason Josephson-Storm's *The Myth of Disenchantment* (2017) goes further, demonstrating that Britain, France, and Germany were experiencing occult and spiritualist revivals at the very moment their intellectuals were producing theories of a \"disenchanted\" modernity. The founding figures of the human sciences \"were not only aware of, but profoundly enmeshed in, the occult milieu.\" Max Weber's famous concept of *Entzauberung* (disenchantment of the world) described an aspiration, not an accomplished fact.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Freemasonry functioned as the primary vehicle for this occultation. The lodges were simultaneously rationalist and esoteric — promoting Enlightenment values of tolerance and free inquiry while practicing rituals with Hermetic, Kabbalistic, and Egyptian symbolic content. Under Napoleon, **French Masonic lodges grew from 300 to over 1,200**, with 22 of Napoleon's 30 Marshals documented as Freemasons, alongside 5 of 6 members of the Imperial Military Council and 6 of 9 ministers. Napoleon's 1798 Egyptian campaign — which produced the *Description de l'Égypte* (24 volumes with over 800 engravings) and the discovery of the Rosetta Stone — triggered an explosion of Egyptomania across Europe that fed directly into Masonic and occult Egyptian symbolism.","styles":{}}]}]

[{"type":"heading","props":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"[[position-1|#1]] — Zarathustra: The First Naming","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The first to explicitly name the cosmic moral duality — Ahura Mazda (Lord of Wisdom/Light) against Angra Mainyu (the destructive spirit). The Zoroastrian revelation, dating to somewhere between 1500–500 BCE depending on scholarship, but in any case the earliest explicit articulation of the archetypal struggle that the whole series maps.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Zarathustra IS the first differentiation of the light principle: he splits the world into truth (*asha*) and lie (*druj*) and makes this split the organising principle of reality. Where [[unit-spectral-devils-chain|Mithra at #1]] manages the BALANCE between the two sides through the act of sacrifice, Zarathustra names the LIGHT SIDE of the split and calls for alignment with it. The naming and the managing are two faces of the same act of first differentiation — one from the light chain, one from the shadow chain.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Historical grounding:** The Zoroastrian framework is the direct ancestor of the Jewish-Christian-Islamic apocalyptic tradition. The cosmic struggle between good and evil, the coming saviour, the final judgement, the restoration of the world — all of these are Zoroastrian before they are Jewish or Christian. The two fish of Pisces — the Age that defines the Christ/Antichrist dialectic — have their origin in Zarathustra's original naming of the two principles. Jung's *Aion* traces how this initial differentiation (Zarathustra's naming) becomes the Christian drama (Christ and his shadow).","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The placement matters historically: Zarathustra at [[position-1|#1]] grounds the entire system in the earliest available mythic articulation of the struggle. Everything that follows — Prometheus, Christ, Jesus, the God-Man — is a development of what Zarathustra first named. The naming does not CREATE the duality (which is eternal, rooted in [[self-identity|Self-Identity's]] own self-differentiating nature) but it makes it CONSCIOUS. Before Zarathustra, the struggle was lived but not articulated as such. After Zarathustra, it has a name and a direction.","styles":{}}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"---","styles":{}}]}]
